implementationState: Initial eight findings committed and pushed; remaining four findings implemented and dynamically validated as an uncommitted continuation

A05.observation: Native cancel buttons have localized download-specific names. Enter/Space each dispatch one abort for the intended synthetic ID; native progressbar names retained. No live download aborted.

A06.observation: Carousel buttons are exposed in the accessibility tree. Enter moves right and enables Left; Space moves back and disables Left at start. Verified in fixture and live Home.

A07.observation: Refresh and pagination use one named native button per action. Four pagination controls follow DOM tab order and dispatch distinct navigation routes. Missing links/page-boundary buttons are disabled and cannot dispatch on click. Both refresh keyboard activations verified against existing loopback OPDS catalog; no remote transaction.

A09.observation: APIAPP results are ordinary named buttons with aria-pressed. Enter/Space select one result without submitting or closing the dialog; Add remains the explicit submission control. Synthetic API response only. Full-height result buttons preserve two-line labels.

A10.observation: One native radio per profile, shared group name, localized named radiogroup, unique DOM IDs and visible-title accessible names. Arrow keys update checked state/focus and Space selects once using real reducer; vanilla inspected live without activating a profile.

A21.observation: Existing toolbar/content skip headings now declare aria-level=2 in both windows. Programmatic focus remains available on both targets. Native screen-reader heading navigation not exercised.

A25.observation: TTS preview details no longer hides its focusable summary. Enter/Space opens/closes preview in fixture and live TTS options; Chromium AX exposes the expanded disclosure. Escape restores TTS options trigger. No audio played.

A29.observation: Description disclosure is exposed, reports aria-expanded and controls the unique description wrapper ID. Enter/Space expands/collapses in both runtime fixtures.

A12.observation: Notifications have native Details, Copy notification and Close buttons. Details exposes expanded/controls state; copy success/failure is a polite status. Visible messages persist until dismissed, including beyond the old five-second timeout with no focus and after blur. Keyboard copy tests record the complete message through a temporary clipboard stub; OS clipboard preserved. Both renderer fixtures and a real Library notification tested. Native screen-reader listening remains unverified.

A22.observation: Library navigation list now directly contains list items, with Settings kept at the bottom. Reader toolbar uses a div for the group layout and valid ul/li groups; its decorative separator is a hidden presentation list item. Static structure and live EPUB/PDF/Library checks pass. Audiobook and Divina conditional branches source-reviewed only.

A23.observation: Docked roots have their own overlay state, stable panel ID and named region. Trigger aria-controls resolves to the displayed region; closed triggers omit controls and report expanded=false. Modal composition retains React Aria behavior. Both Navigation and Reader settings verified live on both dock sides and as modal; reopened modal retains Tab focus and Escape restores the header trigger.

A24.observation: All/None native buttons are siblings of summary inside each details, with filter-specific accessible names. Enter/Space disclosure and bulk selection are independent for tag/color/type/creator in populated fixtures. Empty tag/creator actions are disabled. Live color filter actions tested on empty annotation list and initial selection restored; no note saved or deleted.

limitations: Service-boundary stubs documented per finding; no OS clipboard mutation or real lending/loan/download transaction. No native screen-reader listening or full conformance assertion. A17 content review, A15/A16/A27 risks, A26 reflow/zoom, A31 target size and other format-specific assessments remain. Continuation is uncommitted; original and published evidence preserved.
